item.title: Laparoscopic Versus Open Liver Resection for Colorectal Liver Metastases : An Individual Participant Data Meta-analysis of Four Randomized Clinical Trials.
item.author: Olij B, Pilz da Cunha G, Pugh SA, Abu Hilal M, Lopez-Lopez V, Aghayan D, Brusadin R, Fichtinger RS, Ratti F, Kuemmerli C, Sijberden JP, Besselink MG, Troisi RI, Brandts L, Primrose JN, Edwin B, Robles-Campos R, van Dam RM, Fretland ÅA, LLR vs OLR IPDMA Collaborators.
item.description:
Background Randomized clinical trials (RCTs) have compared laparoscopic liver resection (LLR) and open liver resection (OLR) for colorectal liver metastases (CRLM); however, long-term outcomes and subgroup effects have not been comprehensively evaluated. Purpose To compare postoperative and long-term oncologic outcomes after LLR versus OLR for CRLM using individual participant data from RCTs. Data sources PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from database inception through March 2025 for RCTs comparing LLR and OLR for CRLM. Study selection Eligible studies were RCTs comparing LLR and OLR for CRLM. Data extraction Individual participant data, including unpublished data, were obtained from trial investigators of all 4 published RCTs. item.title: Obesity and Cancer Risk in Young Adults in Korea : A Nationwide Health Screening Cohort Study.
item.author: Yun JS, Mun H, Jung JH, Park Y, Kim SY, Kim K, Ko SH, Ahn YB, Kwon HS, Han K, Son JW.
item.description:
Background Obesity and early-onset cancer are both increasing among young adults, yet evidence remains limited. Objective To assess associations between obesity and early-onset cancer risk in young adults. Design Nationwide population-based cohort study. Setting Korean National Health Insurance Service database, 2009 to 2021. Patients 6 313 338 adults aged 20 to 39 years without prior cancer, from a national health screening program. Measurements Body mass index (BMI) was categorized into 5 groups (underweight to class II obesity) according to Asian-specific criteria. The outcome was incident cancer. Results During a mean follow-up of 11.2 years, 151 893 cancer cases occurred. item.title: Impact of Unrestricted Artificial Intelligence Scribe Deployment in a Single Health System on Clinician Workload and Productivity : A Quality Improvement Study.
item.author: Booth SE, Gould R, Cibotti N, Fields R, Horng S, Jegadeesan V, Li S, Narayan D, Rubins DM, O'Donoghue AL, Simrak A, Stevens JP.
item.description:
Background Ambient artificial intelligence (AI) medical scribes may reduce documentation burden and clinician burnout. Whether use intensity drives benefits remains uncertain. Objective To evaluate the association between AI scribe (Heidi) enrollment and documentation burden and whether changes differ by use intensity. Design Retrospective quality improvement study using an interrupted time series (ITS) indexed on each clinician's enrollment month adjusted for patient demographics and visit complexity. A secondary 3-group ITS compared enrolled nonusers, low users, and high users. Setting 14-hospital health system in Boston, Massachusetts.
